terms.comment: Lewis & Short: a public servant, the paid staff of the magistrates (clerks, lictors, messengers, heralds). Unlike the magistrates, they were salaried and stayed on from year to year, as a civil service does. Levi and Bini give it for a junior state employee (p. 33).
The clerks who kept the public accounts and records, a respected order (Cic. Verr. 2.3.183; Lewis & Short). Traupman’s word for a clerk.

phrases.latin: Est vērō honestus, quod eōrum hominum fideī tabulae pūblicae perīculaque magistrātuum committuntur.
phrases.english: It is indeed a respected order, for the public accounts and the magistrates’ liabilities are entrusted to these men’s honesty.
